newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coal union leader says goals reached.
newsitem.headline: German coal union leader says goals reached.

text.p: German coal miners union leader Hans Berger said on Thursday a compromise on subsidies reached with Chancellor Helmut Kohl was a success that met the union's goals and avoided mass layoffs.

Berger, speaking at a news conference in Bonn televised directly to protesting miners in nearby Cologne, said Bonn had assured the coal industry would survive despite plans to cut overall aid by more than half by the year 2005.
"The fight was worth it," Berger said.

Protesting miners, who besieged Bonn for three days but withdrew to Cologne to allow the talks to proceed in a peaceful atmosphere, were either confused by the complicated compromise or angered that Berger had agreed to some pit closures.

Under the deal, the federal government agreed to provide more aid for the coal industry than planned for the next few years but stuck to its original goal to slash subsidies from over nine billion marks now to 3.8 billion ($2.2) by 2005.

The union said the original plan would cut 50,000 of the 90,000 jobs in the German coal mining industry, which produces coal at three times the world market price and needs the subsidies to keep afloat.
